article_title: The Integration of the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning into the Discipline of Communication Sciences and Disorders
citation: Friberg, Jennifer; Hoepner, Jerry K.; Sauerwein, Allison M.; and Mandulak, Kerry (2023) "The Integration of the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning into the Discipline of Communication Sciences and Disorders," Teaching and Learning in Communication Sciences & Disorders: Vol. 7: Iss. 1, Article 10. https://doi.org/10.30707/TLCSD7.1.1675490380.873306
title: 4M Framework of SoTL impact levels
description: The 4M Framework, first described by Weston and colleagues (2008) and expanded by Simmons (2009), organizes SoTL work by level of impact. It "characterizes SoTL work as occurring in and having impacts at four distinct levels: micro (individual/classroom), meso (department/program), macro (institution), and mega (cross-institutional/disciplinary)." The authors use it to map existing SoTL supports in CSD at the mega, macro, and meso levels, where systematic supports are developed and sustained.
requirements: SoTL work must be positioned at a defined level of impact for the framework to characterize its depth of impact
constraints: The authors identified supports only at the mega, macro, and meso levels, recognizing these as where systematic supports are developed and sustained
target_learners: speech-language pathology and audiology instructors and teacher-scholars in higher education
target_learning_goals: evidence-informed teaching and learning in speech-language pathology and audiology
examples: The authors used the framework to organize their survey of supports across discipline, institution, and program levels, illustrated in Figure 4
